subject.title: [Feature]: Improve `openclaw config` to avoid secrets and invalid files

question: Should interactive bare `openclaw config` remain a documented wizard alias, and should literal writes to SecretRef-capable credential paths remain allowed, warn, or fail unless explicitly overridden?
rationale: Both choices alter public CLI compatibility and credential-handling policy; current main deliberately supports the wizard alias and plaintext values while offering safer additive paths.

options.title: Help-first plus warnings
options.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config`, retain `openclaw configure` and `config --section` as explicit wizard paths, and warn before literal writes to recognized credential paths while recommending SecretRefs.

options.title: Keep wizard alias
options.body: Preserve current root behavior and improve help text and secret-safe examples without changing compatibility or plaintext-write policy.

options.title: Strict credential writes
options.body: Require SecretRefs for recognized credential paths unless an explicit unsafe override is supplied, accepting script and upgrade compatibility costs.

recommendation.title: Help-first plus warnings
recommendation.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config`, retain `openclaw configure` and `config --section` as explicit wizard paths, and warn before literal writes to recognized credential paths while recommending SecretRefs.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad config CLI, setup UX, and write-back history makes this the strongest available owner for the cross-cutting product decision.
